reader.requirement: A sequential READ must select its record from the file position indicator: unsuccessful (46) when no valid next record is established (after an at end or other unsuccessful READ); at end (10) on the first READ of an absent OPTIONAL file; after OPEN the first record; after a READ the next record by record number; at end (10) when none remains; and on success set the indicator to that record's number.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility: at 1985 no file sharing / record lock arbitration around the governed READ; at 2023 the lock checks run. Record selection by the file position indicator is not switched
PREVIOUS refused below 2002, so a 1985 READ always moves forward unless OPEN REVERSED (accepted only at 1985, construct open-reversed-removed-2002) set SequentialConnector.Reversed

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|DialectBehavior' over SequentialConnector.cs and FileConnector.cs: SequentialReadGuard and ReadRecord have no edition test; the edition reaches the connector only through SharingFacilityInEffect (locking) and the 1985-only REVERSED phrase
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 1985 there is no PREVIOUS phrase and no file-sharing lock check, and OPEN INPUT REVERSED (1985 only) reverses the record-number order; the selection rules a-d themselves are the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover the absent-OPTIONAL 10 then 46 arm, 46 after at end and OPEN of an optional file; the I-O mode REWRITE-then-READ ordering, an empty present file, reopen reset, and the REVERSED order are not exercised

reader.notes: SequentialReadGuard tests open mode (47), then the GR12 poison (46), then absent OPTIONAL (10), so the first-time-only 10 and the 46 that follows come out in the 1985 order; ReadRecord selects forward by ordinal, or backward under OPEN REVERSED. Every probe leg matched the 1985 text. Tooling aside: cite.py suggested the designator GRL2.4e.2 for the 46 text but then rejects that designator; GRL2.4 checks OK.

refuter.evidence: Attacked GR4a/GR12's scope: only an UNSUCCESSFUL READ poisons the indicator; an unsuccessful REWRITE must not, and a 04 READ is successful. fpi2.cob at --std 85 (runs/fpi2-001), varying sequential file in I-O mode: REWRITE before any READ -> 'USE VF 43 / K0 43', then READ selects record 1 'K1 AAAAA 00' (indicator from OPEN, GR4c); REWRITE of a wrong-length record -> 'USE VF 44 / K2 44', then READ selects record 2 'K3 BBB 00' and 'K4 CCCCCCC 00' (GR4d, not 46). Absent OPTIONAL file opened I-O (§1985:VII.4.3.4 GR21 creates it): 'O0 05 / O1 AE 10 / O2 46'; reopened INPUT now present and empty: 'P0 00 / P1 AE 10'. gr11c.cob: a 04 READ (truncated record) is followed by the next record 'C2 ... ST=04', 'C3 ... ST=00' (no 46). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR4  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR12  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR12'; 'OK  §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR21  (4.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR21'.
